page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v4 is an entry-level memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with 2 threads on an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512 (Foundation and VNNI), AES-NI, and BMI2. The instance includes 35 MB of shared L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache per core. There is no bundled local storage and no dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes show that compute and multi-threaded throughput are constrained by the dual-vCPU footprint. The instance scored 1268.0 on Geekbench single-core, demonstrating average per-core performance, but Geekbench multi-core reached 1521.0, placing it in the bottom 10 percent of evaluated instances. Multi-core stress-ng tests yielded 1844.46, and the overall PassMark CPU score was 2230.48. Synthetic tests involving code compilation with clang, ray tracing, and physics simulations similarly register in the lower performance tier. Memory bandwidth achieves 102.76 GB/sec for small cached blocks, while uncached large read and write operations measure 14.18 GB/sec and 11.28 GB/sec, respectively.

In operational benchmarks, the instance registered 1.76 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, alongside 2.05 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 726.39 in PassMark database operations. Small language model (135M) inference reached 102.5 tokens per second for prompt processing and 34.13 tokens per second for generation. From an architectural efficiency perspective, the primary value lies in its high memory density per vCPU rather than parallel compute performance. The lack of local storage requires persistent data to rely entirely on external network storage volumes.

The Azure E2s_v4 instance is well suited for memory-centric, low-concurrency applications that require a higher RAM footprint without demanding heavy CPU utilization. Suitable deployments include small caching tiers, small enterprise relational or in-memory databases, staging environments, and lightweight background workers that process data in memory.
description: Microsoft Azure E2s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. It allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core, 16.0 GB of system memory (8.0 GB per core), 35 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local disk storage or GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the instance yields average single-core Geekbench performance (1268.0) but ranks in the lower tier for multi-threaded tasks, recording a PassMark CPU score of 2230.48 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 1521.0. Memory throughput reaches 14.18 GB/sec for uncached reads, while Redis SET operations sustain 1.76 million operations per second. Designed for cost-efficient memory scaling without excessive compute overhead, the E2s_v4 is targeted at small in-memory caches, lightweight relational databases, and low-concurrency enterprise services.
